item.title: Scorsese’s World Cinema Project #5 Carries Serenity and Chaos
item.description: All the films in Martin Scorsese's World Cinema Project No. 5 showcase filmmakers whose output deserves restoration, but Kummatty offers the most direct and unapologetic sensual pleasures.

item.title: Lucinda Williams Tries to Right What’s Wrong with the World
item.description: The ten tracks on Lucinda Williams' World Gone Wrong are heavy. This ain't no party record. There's too much pain going around in the world.

item.title: Joyce Manor Talk Bars and Candy Bars
item.description: Pop-punk's Joyce Manor have a new album that's a fresh take on their patented sound. "Bands in our scene can have songs from a decade ago blow up on TikTok."

item.title: ElectroMatters: Best Electronic Music of January 2026
item.description: From rough 'n' ready techno to subtle drone, atmospheric footwork to striking synthpop, these are the best electronic records from the past month.

item.title: Furry Lewis Sang the Blues at Sun Records in 1961
item.description: The reissue of Furry Lewis' Back on My Feet Again captures a daylong recording session at Sun Records from 1961.

item.title: ‘Rock Springs’ Plunges to Rock Bottom
item.description: Filmmakers of the horror movie Rock Springs sped past indicators to elevate the subject, drove right over the cliff, and plunged to rock bottom.

item.title: Joyce Manor Embrace Their Pop Sensibilities
item.description: The pop-punk institution Joyce Manor emphasize melody on another hooky collection of melancholy-tinged anthems.

item.title: Tigran Hamasyan Seeks Meaning on Rapturous ‘Manifeste’
item.description: Tigran Hamasyan's Manifeste is a journey, profoundly personal and rooted in the world, seeking purpose within it. It's moving and aurally rapturous.

item.title: When Danny Rapp Hopped onto the ‘American Bandstand’ Stage
item.description: American Bandstand's Dick Clark gave Danny Rapp a framed gold disc for his teen hit "At the Hop". Did teenage life get any better than this?

item.title: Kula Shaker Reflect on a Career Following Sanskrit
item.description: British psychedelic rockers Kula Shaker discuss their lengthy career and a stunning new album that reminds us of rock music's power.
